# D1. The OECD cross-section {#data}

Figure {{< var p.fig_US_OECDdata >}} of the paper sets pension spending and the Bismarckian index of the OECD countries
against their population growth and their income inequality. The countries are the OECD members before 2000 in which
informal employment is low and one public pay-as-you-go system pays the bulk of retirement benefits. The index is
$I = 1/(2-\theta)$ of the design θ: the earnings-linked share of the least-squares line through the public pension
across earnings levels, for men under the rules of 2020 (*Pensions at a Glance 2021*), times one minus the share of
public pension spending on minimum top-ups and tested benefits. Appendix {{< var p.app_oecd26_data >}} of the paper
gives the rule and the measure. The
cross-country test of section {{< var p.sec_esc_crossSection >}} runs on the same countries, Luxembourg, which has no
CSES survey of the propensities to vote, at a flat profile ([C5](esc-oecd26.qmd)). The tabs below the figure give the values behind
each marker with the year each refers to, the provider, dataset and series of every column with the date it was
retrieved, and the pairwise correlations the paper's introduction describes.
